definition: Research into techniques that allow humans (or AI-assisted humans) to effectively supervise and evaluate AI systems whose capabilities may exceed what a human can directly verify.
details: Scalable oversight is a central challenge in AI alignment, since as models tackle increasingly complex tasks, it becomes harder for unaided humans to reliably judge whether outputs are correct, safe, or aligned with intent.
story: Imagine a teacher who used to mark every test by hand, and then the class grows to a million students. She cannot read every answer, so she teaches assistants how to grade, writes clear rules for them, and spot-checks their work instead of doing it all herself. People still make the big calls, even though far more work is being done than any one person could watch. That is the honest way to keep a huge system trustworthy as it outgrows a single pair of eyes. Scalable Oversight is the quiet job of staying in charge of something that has grown too big to watch all at once.
